600.author: eshaoliu
600.body:
## Problem

Issue #589 reports two opaque `run_python` failures before the model finds the lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention. The issue did not include the original exception text. Direct reproduction against lmfit 1.3.4 confirms the likely failures:

- `lmfit.conf_interval(result)` → `TypeError: conf_interval() missing 1 required positional argument: 'result'`
- `lmfit.conf_interval(result.minimizer, result)` on a `ModelResult` → `AttributeError: 'ModelResult' object has no attribute 'minimizer'`
- `MinimizerResult.conf_interval()` → `AttributeError: 'MinimizerResult' object has no attribute 'conf_interval'`

The valid forms are `ModelResult.conf_interval(...)` and `lmfit.conf_interval(minimizer, result)`.

## Changes

- `skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`: adds a version-sensitive API section before the workflow. It gives the two valid lmfit 1.3.4 calls, names the invalid forms, requires an `errorbars` check, and points to the reference before the first call. The output-handling guidance now asks for the installed version and the exact exception instead of a guessed correction.
- `skills/code-engineer/references/lmfit-confidence-intervals.md`: documents the result-type matrix, the exact observed errors, and the `errorbars` failure condition.
- `skills/code-engineer/references/lmfit_confidence_intervals.py`: runnable Michaelis-Menten example covering both fit paths.

No exception is swallowed, and no successful result is fabricated. The executor and runtime error handling are unchanged.

## Validation

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.12.14, lmfit 1.3.4, numpy 2.2.6.

The reference example was run directly and through the bundled executor:

```text
lmfit version: 1.3.4
ModelResult vmax: 12.071
ModelResult vmax stderr: 0.091
ModelResult CI parameters: ['km', 'vmax']
MinimizerResult vmax: 12.071
MinimizerResult vmax stderr: 0.091
MinimizerResult CI parameters: ['km', 'vmax']
```

The invalid `lmfit.conf_interval(result)` path was also run through `skills/code-engineer/scripts/execute.py`. It still emits the real traceback and `TypeError`, with `Exit code: 1`, so the documented failure is not hidden.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED.** The agent/`run_python` timeline and local stack require Linux or macOS per `CONTRIBUTING.md`; this session is Windows 11. I executed the library-level example and the bundled executor path, but not the full product journey. The original session's exception text was unavailable, so the reproduction covers the candidate calling conventions rather than the exact transcript.

Partial fix; keep #589 open until the first-call guidance is verified through the agent/`run_python` path on a supported host.

Refs #589

## Release

Release category: release:fix
GitHub label: pending a maintainer; this contributor account has no upstream write access.
User impact: the code-engineer skill now steers the first lmfit confidence-interval call to the correct 1.3.4 signature and requires checking `errorbars`; failed calls still surface the real exception.
Compatibility and migration: none.
600.head: fix/code-engineer-lmfit-conf-interval-guidance
600.title: fix(code-engineer): steer lmfit confidence intervals to the 1.3.4 API

601.author: HongyeZhou
601.body:
## Summary
After #466, Reviewer defaults on and Specialists no longer flash off while loading, but the **composer Automatic review control** still treated unloaded system Reviewer settings (`undefined`) as capability-off. That produced a misleading “unavailable: Reviewer Specialist is off” title/Off label on the new Session path. This change mirrors the Specialists loading rule for the composer, and adds store/journey coverage for the residual #588 cases (new Session defaults under an existing Project; no false unavailable notice when Reviewer is on).

## What #466 already fixed
- Shared `DEFAULT_REVIEWER_*` / `DEFAULT_SESSION_REVIEWER_*` (on) for new catalogs/Sessions
- One-shot lift of pre-#353 persisted Reviewer-off catalogs
- Specialists UI loading flash (`undefined` vs `false`)

## Leftover gap fixed here
- Composer loading flash / false unavailable presentation while `getReviewerSpecialistSettings` is in flight
- Explicit S3 store coverage: new Session gets current Automatic review defaults without rewriting older Sessions’ saved `false`

## Validation (candidate `8602b669d`)
- Scenario UTs: `AutomaticReviewComposer` 4 passed; Reviewer/store cases including new “new Session under existing Project” passed
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4917 / executed 4917 / passed 4917 (full green on matching tree); tip re-run saw 1 unrelated CAS flake that passed 3/3 isolated retries
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24 / executed 24 / passed 24
- Mocked journey `journey-reviewer-auto-audit`: **passed** (toggle On, no unavailable status when Reviewer on; one-click off + reload; manual Run review; unavailable only when Reviewer off)
- L3 real (`CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend legacy`): MiniMax returned **402** insufficient balance; DeepSeek `deepseek-chat` **planned 9 / executed 9 / passed 9**

## E2E user journeys
- Mocked: `test/journey-reviewer-auto-audit.spec.ts` — Automatic review available without false “Reviewer off” block; one-click off; manual review still works
- Real L3 merge profile: 9/9 passed (DeepSeek)

## Release
Release category: release:fix  
User impact: New/upgraded Sessions no longer briefly (or while settings load) look like Automatic review is blocked by a default-off Reviewer when policy says it should be available.  
Compatibility and migration: none beyond existing #466 catalog migration; intentional persisted `false` values remain unchanged.

Closes #588  
Related to #413
601.head: fix/588-auto-review-ui
601.title: fix(web): stop Automatic review composer flash after #466
